_comment: Counterfactual claims: a rule, a RECORDED incident, and the rule's real detector replayed against that incident's preserved input. Read by modules/rule_compiler/counterfactual.py. WOULD_NOT_BLOCK -- a rule that does not fire on the incident that produced it -- is the finding worth having.
_contract: probe is an argv list run without a shell from the repo root, receiving incident_input on stdin; it must call the SHIPPED detector, never re-implement it. incident_input is preserved verbatim from the cited source, never paraphrased to make a claim pass.
_scope: Only rules this repo can actually replay. 140 of the 149 compiled rules come from global:core/HARD-RULES.md and govern other estates (payment secrets, landing pages, i18n mirrors, storefronts); no detector for those exists here or can. See effect_harness.coverage()['out_of_scope'] -- they are UNMEASURABLE HERE, which is a verdict, not a blank.
